_about: A worked example of a marking kit, for an invented Grade 10 science unit test with two versions. Copy it and replace every value with the test you are writing. The format is in FORMAT.md beside this file; keys that start with an underscore are notes and are ignored.

misconceptions.a: one chloride ion for each calcium ion, so the charges do not balance
misconceptions.c: the subscript is written on the metal instead of the non-metal
misconceptions.d: the symbol for calcium is read as C, which is carbon

misconceptions.b: a gas forming is read as mass lost, although the flask is sealed
misconceptions.c: a solid forming is read as mass gained
misconceptions.d: mass in a closed container is thought to depend on which reaction it is

misconceptions.a: two reactants are read as two substances joining
misconceptions.b: two products are read as one substance breaking apart
misconceptions.c: one ion moving is read as an element replacing another, although both reactants are compounds

misconceptions.a: a larger pH number is read as more acidic
misconceptions.b: any pH number is read as basic
misconceptions.d: the pH scale is read as linear, so a difference of 2 is read as 2 times

B1.1.answer: 2 C2H6 and 4 CO2: 4 carbon atoms on each side

B1.2.answer: 2 C2H6 and 6 H2O: 12 hydrogen atoms on each side

B1.3.answer: 7 O2: 14 oxygen atoms on each side
accept: 3.5 O2 before doubling, if the doubling is then shown

B2.2.answer: Mass is conserved; the carbon dioxide is a gas and left the open dish, so its mass was not weighed.
accept: any wording that says the gas escaped and mass is not destroyed

C1.1.answer: The classmate is not right: melting ice is a physical change, because the water is still water and no new substance forms.

C1.2.answer: A gas forms that was not there before.
accept: a colour change that is not just mixing
heat or light is given off
the change is hard to reverse

C1.3.answer: A different piece of evidence from the list in C1.2.

misconceptions.a: the pH scale is read as linear, so a difference of 3 is read as 3 times
misconceptions.c: a larger pH number is read as more acidic
misconceptions.d: any pH number is read as basic

B1.1.answer: 2 C4H10 and 8 CO2: 8 carbon atoms on each side

B1.2.answer: 2 C4H10 and 10 H2O: 20 hydrogen atoms on each side

B1.3.answer: 13 O2: 26 oxygen atoms on each side
accept: 6.5 O2 before doubling, if the doubling is then shown

B2.2.answer: Mass is conserved; the carbon dioxide is a gas and left the open dish, so its mass was not weighed.
accept: any wording that says the gas escaped and mass is not destroyed

C1.1.answer: The classmate is not right: boiling water is a physical change, because the bubbles are water vapour and no new substance forms.

C1.2.answer: A gas forms that is a new substance.
accept: a colour change that is not just mixing
heat or light is given off
the change is hard to reverse

C1.3.answer: A different piece of evidence from the list in C1.2.
